text:
Toronto has lost five straight on this homestand, all in regulation, something The Hockey News points out hadn't happened at home since 1990-91. The Maple Leafs are 8-11-2, winless in five and outscored 22-9, and our numbers say the slide is real: 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games. The noise is getting louder. Auston Matthews said Jim Hiller often doesn't speak with the team after games, as Daily Faceoff relayed. William Nylander is answering trade talk. Rookie Gavin McKenna's mistakes have been under a spotlight. Our playoff odds for Toronto are down to 4.6%.

Edmonton is the worst possible visitor. Connor McDavid has points in 20 straight games (11 goals, 38 assists), and our numbers give him 93% for a point tonight in the city he grew up near. His wife Lauren addressed the rumors linking him to the Leafs ("We're not going to Toronto," as The Times of India headlined it). Leon Draisaitl, with points in seven straight, is at 50% to score, the top number on the board. Zach Hyman, a former Leaf, is one point from 500. Mike Babcock's Oilers have won three straight, though the chances haven't fully backed it (47% of the expected goals). Their season is a finishing story: +24 goal difference on only +3.3 expected, 20.8 goals more than their shots usually produce. Devon Levi has been steady at +1.5.

In Toronto's net, our numbers project Sergei Bobrovsky, who is at .857 and 4.6 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, all losses. Hiller hadn't named a starter as of Friday, per The Hockey News; Anthony Stolarz was in goal when the Leafs beat Edmonton 7-2 on Oct. 24, a game the chances gave Toronto only 41% of the time. Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve, and Jack Roslovic has filled his power-play spot, with 14 points in ten games.

One matchup to watch: Edmonton's power play (0.81 expected goals a game) against a Toronto team that takes 4.2 penalties a night.
headline: Leafs' skid meets McDavid's streak
